# FDG8070

> DO NOT implement value equality on mutable reference types.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.9.1.2 Equals on Reference Types.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG8070
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

Message: Type '{0}' has value equality but is mutable

FDG8070 reports a class declared in source that overrides Object.Equals, or a record class, when the class or one of its base classes declared in source (the fields of base classes from other assemblies are not seen) has an instance field that is neither readonly nor const (the field of an auto-property with a set accessor counts; an init accessor does not, and neither does the field of an event). State that is mutable through a readonly field of a mutable type is not seen, so coverage is partial. Making the type immutable or removing value equality changes its public API, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

Reference types that implement value equality (e.g., `System.String`) should be immutable. Mutable reference types with value equality can, for example, be “lost” in hashtables when their value (and so the hash code) changes.
